description:
Successor to fz-k22.22 task 2 (investigated + STOPPED with evidence, speculative tie-break reverted). materialize_callable_entry_positions (backend.rs:471) silently skips multi-resolution callables; a position-level disambiguation was BUILT AND TESTED and proven impossible: for enum_predicate_search + enum_take_drop_split the ambiguous entries (e.g. CallableId(11) -> targets specialized RawInt vs RawAtom) share ONE consumer executable whose own argument slot is STILL A TYPE VARIABLE when positions are materialized -- the shared body genuinely receives either specialization depending on the caller; no fact on the TransportPosition can pick.

THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY CARRIES THE ANSWER: entry identity is stamped at CONSTRUCTION sites (per-grounding, unambiguous) and travels IN the runtime value (per-entry identity_fn in the fid slot; interp callable_entry_target resolves by it). The fix: consumption sites in a shared/generic consumer body must DISPATCH THROUGH THE VALUE-CARRIED IDENTITY (runtime entry lookup -> target) instead of requiring a static resolved_entry stamp -- the current hard requirements fail clean: native "materialize direct-only callable CallableId(19) without its upstream resolved entry" (jobs/native.rs), interp "closure call executable=260 function=196 callsite=0 has no resolved entry identity or direct target" (ir_interp/backend.rs). Positions that ARE statically unambiguous keep the static stamp (devirtualized fast path); only genuinely shared consumers go through value identity. This greens enum_predicate_search + enum_take_drop_split run/interp/build (the k22 epic goal). Blocks fz-k22.10 resolution. Evidence + reverted prototype described in fz-k22.22 comments.

Authority diagnosis
The first carrier-ABI prototype proved that marking multi-entry positions late is insufficient. In enum_predicate_search, root local ValueId(77), function 86, is already summarized as one CallableFlowFact with two direct edges: RawInt -> executable 92 and RawAtom -> executable 93. The root-side CallArg and Value positions therefore have no entry to stamp. The lost authority is the producer-grounding/call-flow correlation before CallableFlowFact joins its direct edges. The repair must preserve a distinct value-carried entry identity per contributing grounding through transport packaging; it must not infer one from CallableId, capture shape, or a shared consumer position.

Dispatch-set correction
A callable value can itself be multi-surface: the same capture-free root producer ValueId(77) is invoked at both RawInt and RawAtom surfaces. Therefore a value cannot always carry one per-entry identity. It must carry a callable-dispatch-set identity. Singleton sets can retain the current direct entry fid fast path; multi-entry sets require a generated runtime dispatcher selected by that value identity and its runtime invocation shape, which adapts boxed inputs to the selected target ABI. This preserves value ownership without pretending a shared consumer position or the callable descriptor can choose a target.
title: fz-k22: shared consumer bodies must dispatch closure calls through the VALUE-carried entry identity -- a static position->entry stamp is unrepresentable for type-variable arg slots
